jobs.description:
Dignus Medical specializes in recruiting doctors, specialists and nurses for the healthcare sector across Scandinavia. We help solve staffing challenges by matching the right professionals with the right employers – at the right time. This year, we proudly celebrate our 20th anniversary. Watch our anniversary film (https://vimeo.com/1114843079?share=copy) and join us on our journey!
Are you looking for a meaningful specialist position where you can combine professional development with a high quality of life?
This is an opportunity to work within child and adolescent psychiatry in a close-knit Nordic healthcare environment, while living in a peaceful island community surrounded by nature and the sea.
About the Island
This Nordic island is home to approximately 30,000 residents and offers a safe, peaceful and family-friendly environment. With its beautiful archipelago, clean air and easy access to outdoor activities such as hiking, sailing and cycling, the island provides excellent opportunities for an active lifestyle outside of work.
For professionals considering relocation with their families, the island offers schools, daycare services and a welcoming community within a compact geographical area.
About the psychiatric service
The child and adolescent psychiatric service covers the entire island and serves approximately 5,900 children and adolescents aged 0–17.
The service is primarily outpatient-based and currently has around 140 active patients, with approximately 210 referrals per year. About 50% of referrals relate to neurodevelopmental conditions, making ADHD and autism an important part of the clinical work.
Common psychiatric conditions include:
Depression
Anxiety disorders
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
ADHD
Autism
Other child and adolescent psychiatric conditions

Treatment includes psychological and psychotherapeutic interventions, pharmacological treatment, psychoeducation and support for both patients and their families.
When needed, the team also collaborates with schools, social services and other healthcare providers.
About the Role
As a specialist in child and adolescent psychiatry, you will have a broad and varied clinical role with the opportunity to follow patients throughout their assessment and treatment.
Your responsibilities will include:
Assessing, diagnosing and treating children and adolescents with a broad range of psychiatric conditions
Working with both general psychiatric and neurodevelopmental conditions, including ADHD and autism
Developing and following up individualized treatment plans
Providing pharmacological treatment when appropriate
Working closely with psychologists, nurses, social workers and other healthcare professionals
Collaborating with families, schools, social services and other healthcare providers when needed
Participating in clinical discussions and contributing your specialist expertise to the multidisciplinary team
Supporting and mentoring residents and junior doctors
Contributing to the continued development of the psychiatric service

Physicians typically see approximately 4–5 patients per day, alongside clinical rounds, acute assessments and other outpatient responsibilities.
There may also be opportunities for further professional development and increased responsibility within the organization.
Outpatient Work and Acute Psychiatry
The work is predominantly outpatient-based. The child and adolescent psychiatric service does not have its own inpatient ward or separate on-call service.
Acute cases are primarily handled through a reserved acute appointment at the outpatient clinic each week. Other urgent cases may present through the emergency department or psychiatric inpatient services.
When required, the initial assessment can be carried out by the on-call physician within adult psychiatry, in consultation with the child and adolescent psychiatric team.
If a patient requires inpatient care, this is arranged in cooperation with adult psychiatry or the paediatric department, depending on the patient's age, clinical needs and availability.
This structure allows you to focus primarily on planned outpatient psychiatric care while still being involved in acute assessments when required.
Requirements
We are looking for a specialist who:
Holds an EU-recognized specialist qualification in child and adolescent psychiatry
Has broad clinical experience in assessing and treating psychiatric conditions in children and adolescents
Is comfortable working with neurodevelopmental conditions such as ADHD and autism
Can work independently while also enjoying close multidisciplinary collaboration
Has strong communication skills and a patient- and family-centered approach
Is interested in contributing to the professional development of colleagues and junior doctors
Communicates well in English and is motivated to learn Swedish

Why consider this opportunity?
Work-life balance: Outpatient-based work with no dedicated on-call duties within the child and adolescent psychiatric service.
Broad clinical role: Work across child and adolescent psychiatry, with significant exposure to ADHD, autism and other psychiatric conditions.
Collaborative environment: Join a close multidisciplinary team and contribute with your specialist expertise.
Nordic island lifestyle: Enjoy a safe, family-friendly community surrounded by nature and the sea.

What Dignus Medical Offers You
Relocating to another country is a major decision. We will support you throughout the process, from first contact until you are established in your new position.
We offer:
Personal and ongoing support from your dedicated recruiter
Assistance with authorization and specialist recognition when required
Support throughout the relocation process
Assistance related to accommodation and practical relocation matters
Support for accompanying family members
Access to language training with a private tutor via Teams or Skype

Take the Next Step in Your Career
If you are a specialist in child and adolescent psychiatry looking for an opportunity to combine meaningful clinical work with a different way of life, this could be the right next step for you.
Apply today or contact us to learn more about the position and life on this unique Nordic island.
You can also register your CV (https://dignusmedical-en.recman.page/login) or sign up for our newsletter (https://www.dignusmedical.no/en/sign-up-for-newsletter/) to stay updated on future opportunities.

THE OPPORTUNITY IN A NUTSHELL

You? A results-driven sales leader who knows the automotive industry, from working in it or with it. You understand how value is created for car dealers, importers and OEMs, and you thrive leading in change.

Role? You will lead our Swedish Advisory team within Mobility: the Key Account Managers who advise Sweden's largest car dealer groups, importers and OEMs on how to get the most value from Blocket (Vend). You will own the team's results, implement sales strategies and drive a group of experienced Key Account Managers to deliver great commercial outcomes, while leveraging our position as trusted advisors. You will also be part of the Nordic Advisory leadership group, shaping how we develop across Norway, Denmark and Sweden.

Company? Vend, home of FINN, Blocket, Tori, Oikotie, DBA & Bilbasen, where millions of people across the Nordics connect to find what they need.

Location? Join us in our central and modern Stockholm office (hybrid, with remote work flexibility).Why us? Blocket is the leading marketplace for cars in Sweden, and our Advisory team works with the biggest and most strategic players in the industry. This is your chance to lead a team with real market impact, a strong customer base, and a clear Nordic strategy to execute on.

WHO ARE YOU?

A proven results driver: You have documented experience leading commercial teams, and are used to coaching and motivating teams to develop. You are forward-leaning, able to set clear priorities and lead by example.

Industry experience and full value chain understanding: You have experience from the automotive industry or adjacent markets. You understand the full value chain and how the dots connect between OEMs, importers, dealers and consumers. You know how value is created within the industry and how decisions are made.

Digital products or services: You have experience with digital products and/or advertising (Display, Programmatic, Content) from Sales, Strategy, Product or Business Development.

Comfortable with change: You have led teams through change and know how to bring people along. Working with AI and evolving technology is a natural part of how you work - we expect you can be a key part of driving adoption in the team.

Data-driven commercial mindset: You actively use data as part of your leadership and are able to take meaningful actions - always with a human touch. You are able to use trends and insights to create real customer value and compelling narratives.

A trusted senior partner: You build long-term relationships with senior decision-makers and are used to handling complex negotiations. You lead by example, and supporting your team in key customer dialogues comes naturally for you.

A Nordic team player: You collaborate easily across departments and borders, and see real value in learning from and sharing with the Advisory teams in Denmark and Norway.

Fluent in Swedish and English, written and spoken.

WHAT'S THE JOB LIKE?

The Mobility Vertical

At Vend’s Mobility vertical, we are more than 200 motivated experts across the Nordics, on a mission to empower people to make smart mobility choices. Our family of brands includes FINN, Blocket, Bytbil and DBA/Bilbasen, as well as C2B auction platforms Nettbil and AutoVex.

The Sales organisation consists of over 60 dedicated professionals across Oslo, Copenhagen/Århus and Stockholm - split into four departments: Advisory, Outbound, New Car and B2B Marketing. This role will be situated in the Advisory Sales team at Blocket.se and reports directly to the Nordic Advisory Director for the Mobility vertical.

In Advisory Sales, long-term relationships and value-driven sales dialogues are the foundation of everything we do. Through unique data and insights, our goal is to help dealers and OEMs improve their ROI and grow their market share. In our department, we value close collaboration, enjoy working together both digitally and in person, and make sure to create regular opportunities to meet and learn from each other.

The role

The automotive industry is undergoing substantial change driven by digitization of car sales and electrification of the car fleet. As a response to this change, we are introducing deep vertical products across the Nordics, helping customers make smarter choices and optimize their business. As a key part of taking these offerings to the Swedish market, while strengthening our position as trusted advisors, we are now looking for a Sales Manager to lead the Swedish Advisory Sales team.

As Advisory Senior Sales Manager, you will lead your own team of Key Account Managers and specialists. Your key responsibilities will be:

Results and commercial ownership: Own the Swedish Advisory team's revenue. Set clear priorities and coach the team in delivering on classifieds and advertising targets.

Sales management: Develop and execute strategic sales tactics focused on both client value and revenue growth. Stay on top of KPIs and contribute to monthly financial reviews and forecasts.

Team leadership: Lead, motivate, and develop a team of senior profiles. Contribute to a forward-leaning, positive and collaborative team culture.

Leading the transformation: Turn our Nordic Advisory strategy into action in Sweden, and lead the team through change as the industry, our offering and the way we sell evolve. Adopt AI-driven solutions and ways of working as a key responsibility.

Strategic customer partnerships: Be the senior face of Blocket (Vend) and join key customer meetings, support your team in complex negotiations and help customers see where Vend creates value in their business.

Do you love designing clean game architecture, building multiplayer systems that run smoothly, and helping a team of programmers make the right technical decisions? Great! Let's talk.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're building something unannounced, exciting, thoroughly goofy, and built to be played together online. We're now looking for a Lead Game Programmer to help building the underlying systems that make it all work, from the core architecture to the multiplayer tech that connects our players. You'll stay hands-on in the code and the Unity editor while helping the programming team make good technical decisions, stay aligned, and build systems that support creative experimentation. And just to be very clear: this is a technical leadership role, not a people-management position.

Here's what that looks like day to day

In collaboration with game designers, artists, and other programmers, you'll build new features and systems and continuously iterate on improvements. We all work in Unity with C#, with every team member hands-on in the editor

You'll set and communicate the project's technical direction, turning creative goals and production needs into clear technical priorities

You'll help the programming team make architectural decisions, align around shared patterns, and navigate trade-offs between long-term code health and short-term needs

You'll review and improve technical solutions, share best practices, and support other programmers without becoming a gatekeeper or bottleneck

You'll proactively identify technical risks, messy systems, and missing foundations, and take responsibility for addressing them at the right time

Overall, you'll make sure the project is technically healthy and maintain the codebase in a way that makes it easy for others to build on

This includes things like...

Designing an architecture that allows for easy gameplay implementation and flexibility

Implementing and maintaining online features such as matchmaking, invites and friends

Profiling and improving network performance, bandwidth and latency, and making sure the game holds up on real-world connections

Breaking down complex technical challenges, helping decide what to prioritise, and ensuring important decisions are understood by the people they affect

Staying close to the actual game: writing production code, debugging difficult problems, and improving systems as the project evolves

You're a great match if

You have at least ten years of professional game development experience across multiple shipped games and different stages of development, including significant technical ownership or leadership on a project

You have experience setting technical direction and helping a programming team make and implement architectural decisions, with strong judgment in balancing flexibility, maintainability, performance and the needs of a creative production

You're highly proficient in C# and have deep knowledge of the Unity engine and editor

You've shipped at least one online multiplayer game, had real ownership of its networking/online systems, and have hands-on experience with a Unity multiplayer framework (e.g., Coherence)

You communicate clearly and can explain technical decisions and trade-offs to programmers and non-programmers alike

Nice to haves

You have experience shipping iOS and macOS apps, including hands-on integration of Apple platform services such as GameKit and the Game Controller framework using Xcode and Swift

Experience with backend services, dedicated servers or cloud hosting for online games

Interest in multiplayer game design and social features

Experience working with automated build pipelines such as Jenkins

Experience building systemic or open-world games

What always matters to us at Triband

You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward

You're motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness and creativity while actively contributing to sustaining that culture

You believe games are made by teams, not rockstars and that great ideas can come from anyone

You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them

You love exploration and experimentation but don't get too precious when the evidence tells you you're wrong

You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place to be

Practicalities

We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

For this role we also consider people located outside of Denmark and provide financial (and moral!) support with visa application and relocation.

We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

Our working language is English.

We offer

Silly but ambitious projects, and the chance to work on and impact great games that reach millions of players.

A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged.

Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games.

A professional development budget to invest in your growth.

Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, team events, you name it.

Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

Six weeks of vacation (five standard plus one extra on us).

Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement.

Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked.

Pension plan and private health insurance.

Endless amounts of Faxe Kondi.

Compliance will be the number one priority in everything you deliver. You will be expected to work with a strong control mindset, ensuring that payroll and HR processes are accurate, documented and performed in accordance with applicable legislation, collective agreements, internal policies and company standards.
Your key responsibilities will include:
Ensure accurate, compliant and timely end-to-end payroll delivery for both white-collar and blue-collar employees during the transition to the future Payroll Operating Model.  
Maintain strong payroll controls, reconciliations and data-quality checks, ensuring compliance with Swedish legislation, collective agreements, internal policies and company standards.

 What are we looking for? 
At least five years of hands-on experience working independently with Swedish payroll, with a strong understanding of payroll processes, controls and statutory requirements.  
A strong compliance and control mindset. You are structured, thorough and understand that accuracy, confidentiality and adherence to requirements always come first.  
Good knowledge of Swedish payroll legislation and collective agreements, ideally with experience of both white-collar and blue-collar payroll.  
Experience with payroll and HR systems. Previous experience with Kontek Lön, Kontek HRM and/or SAP SuccessFactors is considered an advantage.  
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, combined with good technical understanding and the ability to identify root causes and resolve payroll or system-related issues.  
Comfortable working in a changing environment, with the flexibility and curiosity to move from hands-on payroll processing towards payroll coordination, governance and broader HR responsibilities.  
Strong stakeholder and communication skills, with the ability to explain payroll-related matters clearly and professionally to employees, managers and other stakeholders.  
Fluency in Swedish and English, both written and spoken. 

 What we offer you?

Our range of benefits varies by country and includes diverse health plans, initiatives for work-life balance, transportation support, and a flexible holiday plan with additional incentives

Job Description
Do you have experience in chemical product regulatory compliance and enjoy turning complex legislation into practical solutions? Are you motivated by applying your regulatory experience across global markets and helping the business bring compliant products to our customers? Then this could be the opportunity for you!  

WHAT YOU'LL DO  
We are now looking for a Product Compliance Specialist with a strong regulatory background and experience in chemical products (e.g. scented candles, room scents, glue). In this role, you will be part of the Product Compliance team and focus on chemical compliance as well as product labelling requirements. 
The Product Compliance department brings together specialists across different areas of product compliance and safety. We are responsible for setting requirements and routines for all products sold by the H&M group, in line with legislation and product safety. We research and find regulatory information concerning product safety and legal requirements in new, as well as established markets, and for new products. By supporting several parts of our business with our expertise, we contribute to the overall customer experience. 
In this role you will have a broad end-to-end responsibility, securing requirements connected to product, ingredients, labelling and product reporting. The main responsibilities will include:  
Monitor legislation for chemical products on existing selling markets and ensure that H&M Group’s internal requirements and routines are up to date 
Research requirements for chemical products to enable expansion, for new markets and new products 
Secure compliance with REACH and REACH-like regulations, e.g. EU REACH, UK REACH, KKDIK; investigate legal requirements on existing- and expansion markets, secure that internal routines for formulated products are up to date and implemented in production, follow-up on quantities and certificates 
Manage mandatory product reporting and notification requirements in designated markets, ensuring timely and accurate submissions to meet critical regulatory deadlines 
Monitor and interpret regulatory requirements for product and online labelling of chemical products, assess their impact on the business, and translate them into clear compliance requirements and guidance. Transform complex regulatory requirements into user-friendly information and guidelines in order to enable compliance. 
Support global authority inspections, audits, and regulatory inquiries by coordinating responses and providing the required information.  
Collaborate with, support and train colleagues and other stakeholders to ensure regulatory requirements are understood and effectively implemented. 

WHO YOU ARE 
We're looking for someone who combines a relevant academic background with hands-on experience from relevant industry and/or working within a regulatory authority. You're comfortable navigating complex regulatory requirements and can translate your expertise into clear, practical guidance for the business. You enjoy taking ownership of your area of expertise while collaborating with different stakeholders and making complex regulatory information accessible to others. 
 
We are looking for a person with... 
A degree in chemistry, toxicology, or similar field 
At least two years' experience working with chemical product regulatory compliance 
Hands-on experience working with CLP and REACH regulations  
Knowledge of the Biocidal Products Regulation is considered an advantage 
Experience working with regulatory requirements for chemical consumer products such as candles, room scents or similar product categories is a strong plus  
Strong communication skills in English (Swedish is considered an advantage)  

And a person who is... 
Driven, adaptable and comfortable applying your expertise to different business needs  
Able to take ownership and work independently while being a strong team player 
Skilled at making complex information simple and accessible, always with the business and customer in mind 
Business and customer-focused, with the ability to balance regulatory requirements with business needs 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 
This is a full-time permanent position based from our Head Office in Stockholm, reporting to the Group Manager for Compliance. If you feel that your experience, skills and ambitions are right for this role, please send your resume in English at your earliest opportunity. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis.  

WHO WE ARE 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make. 
We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together we want to use our power, our scale and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. Read more about us here 

WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE 
At H&M Group we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. 
An example of our benefits: 
25% Staff discount on all our H&M Group brands both in stores and online (H&M, COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories and ARKET). 
H&M Incentive Programme – HIP. Learn more about the programme here. 

JOIN US 
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it is our people who make us who we are. 
Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here. 
We look forward to receiving your application!

We are now looking for a Global Brand Lead to take ownership of the brand on a global level and turn it into one clear strategy, one strong brand team and one consistent expression in every market and every channel.
The roleYou set the strategic direction for the Mips brand, you lead the global brand team that delivers it, and you drive brand awareness across both B2B and B2C audiences. This is a highly cross-functional role: you work with the rest of Marketing, Product and Sales so the brand is expressed consistently and effectively. Lead and develop the global brand team. Lead, coach and develop a team of an Art director, a graphic designer, a content creator and a product marketer, and set clear priorities.

Measure and sharpen. Define and follow up on brand KPIs: awareness, consideration, preference and brand equity. Use the insights to sharpen the strategy and present results to senior leadership.
Be the guardian of the brand. Govern the brand guidelines, approve key assets and support partners and customers in using the brand correctly.
Manage budget and partners. Own the global brand budget and the relationships with external agency partners.

Who you are
You have at least 7+ years of experience in international brand management, head of brand or head of marketing with brand lead, ideally from a similar type of passion driven context.
You have experience of leading a brand team of specialists, including creative and content roles such as designers, content creators and product marketers, with strong people leadership and coaching skills.
You write sharp briefs and know how to work with senior creatives.
You have worked in both B2B and B2C environments and understand how brand building differs between them.
You are strategic: you move from insight and analysis to a clear brand strategy, and then make it actionable.
You have documented experience of building brand awareness and measuring its effect.
You are a strong collaborator who thrives in a cross-functional, matrixed and international organization, with excellent stakeholder management skills and comfort presenting to senior leadership.
You are fluent in English, both written and spoken. Swedish is a strong advantage.

Why Mips? Mips has built a strong position in safety, with a technology trusted by leading brands around the world. Cycling represents around 70% of our sales, while sport, motorcycle and new categories offer exciting opportunities for growth. Europe is a key focus, with Germany as a priority market. Now is the time to build the next chapter of MIPS. If you want a role where you can shape a global brand, build a team and see your ideas come to life across markets, this could be your next challenge.

jobs.description:
Department of Clinical Sciences
Do you have clinical experience as a small animal veterinarian and are a board-certified specialist, or have equivalent qualifications, in animal reproduction? An opportunity has arisen to join the Small Animal Department at the University Animal Hospital (UDS), working with reproduction and general veterinary care in a setting closely integrated with research and the teaching of veterinary-and veterinary nursing students. We look forward to receiving your application!
About the position
As a licensed veterinarian and reproduction specialist at UDS, you will work at the Reproduction Clinic. The clinic provides diagnostic services and treatment for diseases of the reproductive organs, optimisation of mating timing, investigation and management of oestrus cycle disorders, fertility assessments, as well as semen collection and cryopreservation and artificial insemination (AI).
You will also participate in general veterinary care as part of the varied day-to-day activities at Sweden's only university animal hospital, which operates around the clock.
The position includes evening, night and weekend shifts. Our operations run 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
You will receive support from our specialists and experienced colleagues in the team, helping you to feel at home in the clinic and develop professionally in your role.
As SLU is Sweden's only institution providing higher education for animal health professionals, you will play an active role in educating the veterinarians and veterinary nurses of the future, both in the clinical setting and through other teaching activities in animal reproduction.
You will also devote some of your time to reproductive research, with opportunities to apply for your own research funding or participate in other research projects. Our reproductive research is highly active and encompasses all animal species and all aspects of reproduction. The Department has access to advanced laboratory techniques, enabling both in vivo and in vitro studies, and benefits from well-established national and international collaborations.
Your profile
You are a licensed veterinarian authorised to practise veterinary medicine in Sweden. You have several years of clinical experience working at a small animal clinic. You are a Diplomate and a specialist in animal reproduction, with a subspecialty in small animal reproduction (or have equivalent qualifications). We would like you to have experience as a reproduction veterinarian, with the skills required to perform routine procedures such as insemination, semen collection and cryopreservation.
As the position involves extensive contact with animal owners and students, you must have a good command of Swedish, both spoken and written, or have a good proficiency in English and be motivated to learn Swedish. The Department will support you in developing your Swedish language skills.
At the University Animal Hospital, we are customer-focused and committed to maintaining a professional approach characterised by goodwill and a positive attitude in our relationships with clients and colleagues. You are an effective communicator with the ability to establish and maintain good relationships with both clients and colleagues. You have an interest in teaching and in contributing to an environment that provides good conditions for research. As a veterinarian at the University Animal Hospital, you take a scientific approach to your work and have an interest in evidence-based veterinary medicine. You understand that working in an emergency service, where workloads are driven by unpredictable events and working hours are irregular, requires flexibility and adaptability.
As a person, you are well-organised, have good self-awareness and an understanding of what causes you stress, and are motivated to contribute to the organisation. In this recruitment process, great emphasis will be placed on your personal qualities and competencies.
About us
The Department of Clinical Sciences is responsible for undergraduate education, research and postgraduate education in the fields of anaesthesiology, diagnostic imaging, veterinary nursing, epidemiology, laboratory animal science, surgery, clinical chemistry, medicine and reproduction. Our activities in all these fields encompass all animal species.
At the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU), University Animal Hospital (UDS), education, research and advanced veterinary care go hand in hand. 
Under one roof, we provide veterinary care for horses, dogs, cats and other small animals. In addition to modern facilities specifically designed for our operations, we have access to advanced diagnostic imaging equipment and a specialist veterinary diagnostic laboratory.
Read more about our benefits and working at SLU by visiting: https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/work-at-slu/
Location:
Uppsala, Sweden
Form of employment:
Indefinite-term employment. We use 6 months probationary employment.
Scope:
100%
Start date:
As agreed. 
Application:
Please submit your application before deadline 7 December 2026. Applications cannot be submitted through the recruitment system on 20–22 November due to a system update.
Please include in your application: 
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Letter of intent
Copies of appropriate degree certificates

Union representatives:
https://internt.slu.se/en/my-employment/employee-associations/kontaktpersoner-vid-rekrytering/
 
 
The Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) has a key role in the development for sustainable life, based on science and education. Through our focus on the interaction between humans, animals and ecosystems and the responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable societal development and good living conditions on our planet. Our main campuses are located in Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, however, the university also operates at research stations, experimental forests and teaching sites throughout Sweden. SLU has around 4,000 employees, 6,000 students and doctoral students and a turnover of over SEK 4,5 billion. We are investing in attractive environments on all of our campuses. We strive to provide a work environment characterised by inclusivity and gender equality, where different experiences generate conversations between people and pave the way for science, creativity and development. Therefore, we welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

Job Description
As Unit Manager for Identity & Access Management (IAM), you will lead one of H&M Group’s most critical cyber security capabilities and play a key role in strengthening the organisation’s security, resilience and ability to deliver on its strategic ambitions. 
As a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team reporting to the CISO, you will share accountability for the overall cyber security strategy, priorities and long-term development of the Cyber Security function. Working closely with leaders across business, technology and cyber security, you will help shape outcomes that balance business objectives, security needs and risk management across H&M Group. 
You will provide strategic leadership for H&M Group’s global IAM capability through an established leadership team spanning the end-to-end identity lifecycle. Through your leadership, you will drive the continued evolution of IAM, ensuring the capability remains effective, scalable and aligned with the future needs of the business. 
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Lead the strategic direction, maturity and long-term development of H&M Group’s Identity & Access Management capability, defining and evolving the IAM strategy, roadmap and operating model in alignment with business, technology and cyber security objectives. 
Contribute as a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team to the overall cyber security strategy, priorities, operating model and long-term capability development. 
Build strong partnerships with business, technology and cyber security stakeholders to drive alignment, influence decisions and enable strategic outcomes. 
Drive organisational effectiveness, workforce planning, capability development and succession planning within the IAM function. 
Ensure effective management of IAM-related risks, controls, regulatory obligations and strategic initiatives. 
Lead budgeting, resource and investment planning, vendor strategy and prioritisation to support delivery of IAM and cyber security objectives. 
Foster a high-performing, collaborative and inclusive culture focused on continuous improvement, innovation and business value. 

WHO YOU ARE
We are looking for people with:
8+ years of people management experience in cyber security, IAM or a closely related field. 
Proven experience leading an enterprise-scale IAM capability end to end in a global organisation, spanning governance, risk and compliance, architecture, engineering, delivery and operations. 
Proven experience leading through managers and developing high-performing leadership teams, with full ownership of a multidisciplinary organisation and its outcomes. 
Experience as a member of a senior cyber security, technology or enterprise leadership team, contributing to shared strategy, priorities, investment decisions and organisational outcomes beyond the individual’s own area of responsibility. 
Experience defining and executing enterprise IAM strategies, roadmaps, operating models and large-scale transformation, including organisational change across functional and organisational boundaries. 
Strong knowledge of IAM capabilities and technologies, including identity lifecycle management, access governance, authentication, authorisation and privileged access management, as well as enterprise IGA platforms such as Saviynt, SailPoint or similar. 
Strong knowledge of IAM-related risks, controls, policies, regulatory requirements and audit expectations. 
Experience managing significant budgets, investments, resources, sourcing arrangements and external partners, including leading negotiations with strategic vendors. 
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with proven experience engaging senior and executive stakeholders, clearly communicating strategic direction and translating complex IAM, cyber security and risk topics into business implications, priorities and decisions. 
Sound judgement and decision-making capability in complex, uncertain and risk-sensitive situations. 
Relevant certifications in IAM, cyber security or risk management are considered beneficial. 

Additional Information
This is a fulltime permanent role based in Stockholm, Sweden. 
If you believe your experience, skills, and ambitions align with this role, please submit your CV in English.
Diversity, Inclusion, and Innovation 
At H&M Group, we're deeply committed to fostering a Diverse & Inclusive environment. We actively seek out qualified candidates regardless of race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, national origin, disability, or age. 
Our commitment to an inclusive workplace drives our dynamic and forward-thinking culture. Regardless of your background, origin, or preferences, your application is warmly welcomed. We value diverse perspectives and skills, and every applicant contributes to our vibrant, creative community. Join us and be part of the future we're building. 
Our Offer 
At H&M Group, you're not just joining a team – you're joining a value-driven culture and an expansive tech network. Enjoy perks like staff discount cards, flexible work arrangements, wellness benefits, parental support, and more. Here, you're encouraged to be yourself, experiment, and chart your own growth path. As you flourish, so do we, with opportunities to create tangible impacts and shape the future. 
WHO WE ARE 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make. 
We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. 
WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE  
We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET.

What would you do as our Product Owner Revolving Doors.
As Product Owner for our Revolving Door product range, you assume full technical ownership of a comprehensive and established product line. Coordinating a multidisciplinary R&D team spanning hardware, firmware, and mechanical engineering, you will set priorities, drive alignment with portfolio priorities, and create the conditions in which engineers can perform and grow at their best.

Oversee and develop a multidisciplinary R&D team — provide clear direction and hands-on management of hardware, firmware, and mechanical engineers; foster a culture of technical excellence, structured problem-solving, and continuous professional development, while coaching the team toward stronger resolution-making and greater ownership.
Own the full product development lifecycle — drive concept, validation, industrialisation, and ongoing lifecycle improvements, while ensuring consistent adherence to applicable safety and quality standards, including ISO, CE, EN16005, and UL.
Define and execute the R&D strategy — establish the product roadmap, ensure alignment with broader portfolio and business targets, manage R&D resources, budgets, and timelines, and embed sustainability principles across all stages of product development.
Drive innovation and the adoption of emerging technologies — identify opportunities to enhance product performance and design, stimulate creative thinking within the team, and evaluate the application of IoT, connectivity, AI, and other forward-looking technologies across the product range.
Represent the product externally and manage key stakeholder relationships — act as a credible technical ambassador in customer meetings, trade shows, and industry forums, while maintaining strong internal alignment with segment management, commercial product managers, and factory teams.

The skills and experience you need
We are looking for someone who has:
Engineering foundation — a degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related field, combined with a solid background in R&D for electromechanical products gained through hands-on engineering, product development, or early-career coordination roles.
Product lifecycle expertise — demonstrated experience managing the full development lifecycle, from concept and validation through to industrialisation and continuous improvement, with a strong understanding of systems, spare parts, and lifecycle stewardship.
Technical guidance skills— proven ability to lead and coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams, with the capacity to set direction, manage priorities, and drive delivery across hardware, firmware, and mechanical disciplines.
Compliance and quality awareness — familiarity with relevant safety and quality standards such as ISO, CE, EN16005, and UL, and a structured approach to process optimisation and regulatory adherence.
Domain knowledge and technology acumen — familiarity with revolving doors, door mechanics, drive systems, sensors, or embedded control units is a strong advantage. We equally welcome candidates who bring technical curiosity, analytical strength, and the motivation to grow into a product ownership role. An interest in emerging technologies such as IoT, connectivity, and AI is highly valued.

 
You are a natural leader who guides with clarity and purpose — someone who inspires confidence in a team not through authority alone, but through genuine engagement, consistent follow-through, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves when it matters. You think in possibilities, approaching technical tasks with creativity and a structured mind, always looking for smarter ways forward.
You are customer-centric by nature, with a keen sense of how engineering decisions translate into real-world impact — both for end users and for the business. You balance technical depth with pragmatic judgement, knowing when to dive into the details and when to step back and see the bigger picture. Proficiency in spoken and written English and Swedish is essential. Additional languages are a welcome advantage.
Above all, you act with integrity. You take ownership of your work and your team's outcomes, bring a safety-conscious mindset to every resolution, and hold yourself accountable to the highest standards — commercially, technically, and as a supervisor of people.

Learning and career development opportunities, whether it’s online learning, management training or enhancing your skills
A competitive salary and incentive schemes

What we do at Blykalla
Blykalla is a Swedish deep-tech company at the forefront of the nuclear industry, pioneering the development of small modular reactors that provide clean, safe, and reliable energy. Thanks to lead-cooling, we achieve high safety in a very compact format, allowing for a simple and cost-effective design that can be mass-produced. Our unique reactor design will provide safe and green baseload energy that perfectly complements solar and wind power.

What you’ll get to do
We are seeking a Senior Control Systems Engineer with deep expertise in ABB 800xA DCS to lead the development of Blykalla's plant control system architecture and implementation strategy.
This is a unique opportunity to help define the control philosophy of a first-of-a-kind advanced nuclear reactor. You will play a key role in ensuring that Blykalla develops and retains ownership of critical control system intellectual property while working closely with ABB and other suppliers.

Key Responsibilities
DCS Architecture & Ownership
Lead the design and development of Blykalla's plant-wide automation and control system architecture.
Define the ABB 800xA system architecture for reactor, balance-of-plant, auxiliary, and test facility applications.
Develop internal engineering standards, libraries, templates, and control strategies to maximize in-house ownership of intellectual property.
Establish long-term governance for control system design, lifecycle management, cybersecurity, and configuration control.

Control System Engineering
Develop functional specifications, control narratives, cause-and-effect matrices, and automation philosophies.
Design and implement control logic, sequences, interlocks, alarms, and operator interfaces.
Configure ABB 800xA applications, controllers, engineering environments, and HMI systems.
Define communication architectures including OPC UA, IEC 61850, Modbus, Profibus/Profinet, Ethernet/IP, and other industrial protocols.
Develop and maintain simulation and testing environments for control system validation.

Nuclear Plant Integration
Support the integration of reactor systems, safety systems, and balance-of-plant equipment into the overall control architecture.
Work closely with reactor, thermal-hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, and safety engineers to define system requirements.
Contribute to licensing and regulatory documentation related to instrumentation and control systems.
Support development of digital I&C architectures aligned with nuclear industry expectations and international standards.

Vendor & Stakeholder Management
Act as the primary technical interface with ABB regarding 800xA architecture, licensing, engineering tools, and implementation support.
Ensure that Blykalla retains ownership of application software, engineering databases, configuration standards, and control strategies.
Manage external engineering partners and system integrators where required.
Participate in factory acceptance tests (FAT), site acceptance tests (SAT), commissioning, and startup activities.

Verification & Validation
Develop testing methodologies for control logic verification and system validation.
Lead integration testing and commissioning activities.
Support development of digital twins and operator training simulators.
Ensure traceability from requirements through implementation and testing.

You will be part of a highly skilled team with a can-do attitude. We value personnel chemistry and strive to create a workplace where you enjoy coming to. There are however a few things that we think will help in order for you to succeed in this role, these are:
MSc or BSc in Control Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years of experience in industrial automation and control systems engineering.
Extensive hands-on experience with ABB 800xA DCS engineering, configuration, commissioning, and lifecycle management.

Are you an experienced payment sales professional ready to combine commercial leadership with closing strategic deals yourself? Dintero is looking for a Head of Enterprise & Platforms Nordics to bring together its Nordic enterprise sales efforts, develop the team and drive growth across some of the company’s most important customer segments.
About the job
This is a direct recruitment, which means that the recruitment process takes place through Bravura and you are employed directly by Dintero.
About the company
Dintero is a fast-growing Norwegian fintech company challenging traditional payment providers with a modern, fully integrated payment platform. The company is one of few players in the Nordics covering the entire payment value chain and is licensed to process Visa and Mastercard transactions directly, making Dintero Norway’s first new acquirer in more than 20 years.
The offering covers online and in-store payments, Unified Commerce and payment solutions for platforms and marketplaces. With enterprise customers such as Vy and regulatory approval to offer payment services across the EEA, Dintero is positioned for further expansion across the Nordics and Europe. In 2025, the company onboarded more than 2,100 new businesses, increased payment volume by over 150% and revenue by 200%, while reaching profitability in Q4.
You will join a growing Nordic organisation with short decision paths and a high degree of ownership. There are established structures and processes, but these evolve as the business grows. Leaders are expected to identify what can be improved and actively contribute to developing how the organisation works.
Tasks and responsibilities
As Head of Enterprise & Platforms Nordics, you will have commercial responsibility for developing Dintero’s enterprise and platform sales across Sweden, Norway and Denmark. A key part of the role is to bring the three markets together and establish a common Nordic approach to sales, pipeline management and commercial priorities.
This is a player-coach role, particularly during the first year. Alongside leading and developing the team, you will personally work with Dintero’s most strategic customers and drive complex enterprise opportunities from initial dialogue to signed agreement. You will work with senior and C-level decision-makers and navigate longer sales cycles involving both commercial and technical stakeholders.
You will also develop the existing sales team and play an active role in recruiting and building the team further across the Nordics, with the ambition to hire 3–5 additional salespeople during the first 12 months. As the organisation expands, the role will gradually shift towards more leadership and commercial strategy, while maintaining a strong connection to customers and the market.
You will work closely with the CEO, product and technical teams to develop Dintero’s enterprise offering. You are not expected to be a technical specialist, but you need to understand complex payment solutions and be comfortable discussing areas such as APIs, integrations and platform architecture.
Your main responsibilities include:

Lead and develop Enterprise & Platforms sales across the Nordics

Personally drive and close strategic enterprise and platform deals

Coach and develop the existing sales team and recruit additional salespeople

Develop structure around pipeline, sales methodology, CRM and forecasting

Collaborate with leadership, product and technical teams to develop the enterprise offering

Education, experience and personal characteristics
Several years of experience within the payments industry

Proven experience closing complex, high-value enterprise deals in the Nordic market

Previous leadership experience, including people responsibility, coaching, developing and recruiting salespeople

Experience selling both in-store terminal solutions and online/e-commerce payments

Commercial and technical understanding of areas such as APIs and integrations and platform architecture

Existing network within Nordic enterprise retail

Fluent English and at least one Scandinavian language: Swedish, Norwegian or Danish

Experience selling through and building partnerships with e-commerce platforms and integration partners is meritorious

An existing network across marketplace or platform verticals is meritorious

To succeed in the role, you take ownership and are comfortable creating structure while remaining close to sales. As a leader, you coach and give experienced salespeople ownership of their deals while setting clear expectations around execution and results.
You are comfortable in an environment where processes evolve as the company grows. Ovako is one of Europe’s leading manufacturers of advanced engineering steel and has supplied steel for critical industrial applications for nearly 500 years. The company is now making a strategic investment in the defence industry and is looking for someone who wants to play a key role in establishing and developing Ovako’s position in one of Europe’s fastest-growing segments.
At Ovako, you will have the opportunity to combine business development, an understanding of the defence industry and relationship building in a role offering substantial autonomy, high visibility and the opportunity to shape the direction of an entirely new initiative. You will join a stable industrial company with a long-term perspective, Nordic production, strong ownership and a clear ambition to grow within the defence segment.

In the role of Sales Manager Security and Defense, you will be responsible for establishing, developing and strengthening Ovako’s business within the defence industry. This is a newly created role designed to develop Ovako’s long-term position throughout the defence supply chain, from OEMs and systems suppliers to subcontractors and other key players in the segment.

You understand how the defence industry operates, know where decisions are made and can build trust with technical specialists, procurement professionals and business leaders alike. The role requires a high degree of independence, and you will be expected to set your own agenda, take the initiative and drive business forward, even when results may take time to materialise.
You will represent the full Ovako Group offering and work closely with the sales organisation, business units, production and R&D to translate customer needs into long-term business opportunities.

You will join a global organisation with strong industrial owners, Nordic production and a long tradition of innovation, quality and sustainability.
